info.short_name: Flourishing (meets all 3 items), ages 6-17
info.long_name: NSCH: Flourishing for children and adolescents, age 6-17 years: Meets all 3 flourishing items
info.short_description: Flourishing for children and adolescents, age 6-17 years: Meets all 3 flourishing items.
info.long_description: Weighted percent of children in the universe (Children ages 6-17) meeting the Title V definition 'Flourishing for children and adolescents, age 6-17 years: Meets all 3 flourishing items' (Top category of a Title V code variable; Title V code variable flrish6to17). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): K6Q71_R (How often does this child ... Show interest and curiosity in learning new things? Always/Usually/Sometimes/Never); K7Q84_R (How often does this child ... Work to finish tasks they start? Always/Usually/Sometimes/Never); K7Q85_R (How often does this child ... Stay calm and in control when faced with a challenge? Always/Usually/Sometimes/Never). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: 'Always' or 'Usually' on all three items (the Title V code's count of 'Always' or 'Usually' responses equals 3). An unanswered item counts as not met; children with all three items missing are excluded. The Title V code restricts flourishing to data years 2018 onward; 2016-2017 are not reported. This is the 'Meets all 3 flourishing items' category reported by the Data Resource Center for Child and Adolescent Health (childhealthdata.org) for indicator 2.4; pooling 2022 and 2023 with this coding reproduces the DRC national value of 60.4% (39,696 sampled children meeting all 3). Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

info.long_name: NSCH: Flourishing for children and adolescents, age 6-17 years: Meets all 3 flourishing items - poor reliability flag
info.short_description: 1 if the 95% CI of nsch_pct_flourishing_6_17 is wider than 20 percentage points or 1.2 times the estimate; 0 otherwise; NA if no estimate.
info.long_description: Flag following the NSCH Comprehensive Analytic Guide (Data Presentation Standards): 'if the 95% confidence interval width exceeds 20 percentage points or 1.2 times the estimate (relative standard error>30%), flagging the estimate for poor reliability ... is recommended'. The estimate is still reported. When the estimate is exactly 0 or 100 the logit CI is undefined: the CI columns are NA and, as a PopHIVE convention (not part of the Census guidance), the estimate is flagged 1.

info.short_name: Two or more adverse childhood experiences
info.long_name: NSCH: NOM_Adverse Childhood Experiences: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who have experienced 2 or more ACEs
info.short_description: NOM_Adverse Childhood Experiences: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who have experienced 2 or more ACEs.
info.long_description: Weighted percent of children in the universe (Children ages 0-17) meeting the Title V definition 'NOM_Adverse Childhood Experiences: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who have experienced 2 or more ACEs' (National Outcome Measure (NOM); Title V code variable ACE2). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): ACE1 (SINCE THIS CHILD WAS BORN, how often has it been very hard to cover the basics, like food or housing, on your family's income? counted if Somewhat often or Very often) and ACE3-ACE11 (To the best of your knowledge, has this child EVER experienced: parent or guardian divorced or separated; parent or guardian died; parent or guardian served time in jail or prison; saw or heard parents or adults slap, hit, kick, punch one another in the home; was a victim of violence or witnessed violence in their neighborhood; lived with anyone who was mentally ill, suicidal, or severely depressed; lived with anyone who had a problem with alcohol or drugs; treated or judged unfairly because of their race or ethnic group; treated or judged unfairly because of a health condition or disability). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: two or more of the adverse childhood experiences listed (hard to cover basics counts when 'Somewhat often' or 'Very often'; each other item counts when 'Yes'). Answered items are counted even if others are missing; children missing every item are excluded. Title V code comments: ACE5 wording added 'or prison' in 2021; ACE11 (treated unfairly because of a health condition) was added in 2021, so 2016-2020 counts are out of 9 items. Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

info.long_description: Weighted percent of children in the universe (Adolescents ages 12-17) meeting the Title V definition 'NPM_Adolescent Well-Visit: Percent of adolescents, ages 12 through 17, with a preventive medical visit in the past year' (National Performance Measure (NPM); Title V code variable WellVisit_12to17). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): K4Q20R (DURING THE PAST 12 MONTHS, how many times did this child visit a doctor, nurse, or other health care professional to receive a PREVENTIVE check-up?) and S4Q01 (DURING THE PAST 12 MONTHS, did this child see a doctor, nurse, or other health care professional for ... any kind of medical care?). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: 1 or more preventive check-ups in the past 12 months (K4Q20R = 2 or 3). Denominator adds 0 visits (K4Q20R = 1) and adolescents with no health care visit of any kind (S4Q01 = No). Not reported for 2018: the Title V code omits this measure for 2018 ('S4Q01 is not comparable in 2018'). Title V code comment: '2021 starts the inclusion of telehealth visits'. Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

This is the 'Meets all 3 flourishing items' category reported by the Data Resource Center for Child and Adolescent Health (childhealthdata.org) for indicator 2.4; pooling 2022 and 2023 with this coding reproduces the DRC national value of 60.4% (39,696 sampled children meeting all 3). info.short_name: Two or more adverse childhood experiences
info.long_name: NSCH: NOM_Adverse Childhood Experiences: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who have experienced 2 or more ACEs
info.short_description: NOM_Adverse Childhood Experiences: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who have experienced 2 or more ACEs.
info.long_description: Weighted percent of children in the universe (Children ages 0-17) meeting the Title V definition 'NOM_Adverse Childhood Experiences: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who have experienced 2 or more ACEs' (National Outcome Measure (NOM); Title V code variable ACE2). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): ACE1 (SINCE THIS CHILD WAS BORN, how often has it been very hard to cover the basics, like food or housing, on your family's income? counted if Somewhat often or Very often) and ACE3-ACE11 (To the best of your knowledge, has this child EVER experienced: parent or guardian divorced or separated; parent or guardian died; parent or guardian served time in jail or prison; saw or heard parents or adults slap, hit, kick, punch one another in the home; was a victim of violence or witnessed violence in their neighborhood; lived with anyone who was mentally ill, suicidal, or severely depressed; lived with anyone who had a problem with alcohol or drugs; treated or judged unfairly because of their race or ethnic group; treated or judged unfairly because of a health condition or disability). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: two or more of the adverse childhood experiences listed (hard to cover basics counts when 'Somewhat often' or 'Very often'; each other item counts when 'Yes'). Answered items are counted even if others are missing; children missing every item are excluded. Title V code comments: ACE5 wording added 'or prison' in 2021; ACE11 (treated unfairly because of a health condition) was added in 2021, so 2016-2020 counts are out of 9 items. Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

info.short_description: Number of sampled children with a valid (numerator or denominator) value for nsch_pct_adequately_insured in this cell.
info.long_description: Unweighted count of NSCH respondents in the measure's denominator for this geography, year and demographic cell; this is the 'unweighted denominator' to which the NSCH Analytic Guide presentation standard applies. Weighted percent of children in the universe (Children ages 0-17) meeting the Title V definition 'SM_Adequate Insurance: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who are continuously and adequately insured' (Standardized State Performance Measure (SM); Title V code variable AdqIns). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): CURRINS (currently insured), INSGAP (insured all 12 months / with gaps / no coverage past 12 months), K3Q20 (How often does this child's health insurance offer benefits or cover services that meet this child's needs?), K3Q22 (How often does this child's health insurance allow them to see the health care providers they need?), HOWMUCH (out-of-pocket amount paid for this child's care in the past 12 months) and K3Q21B (How often are these costs reasonable?). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: insured all 12 months (INSGAP = 1) and insurance adequate, i.e. benefits (K3Q20) and access to providers (K3Q22) 'Always' or 'Usually' meet needs, and out-of-pocket costs (K3Q21B) 'Always' or 'Usually' reasonable or no out-of-pocket costs (HOWMUCH = $0); an item that is missing does not disqualify. Denominator adds children currently uninsured, uninsured at any point in the past 12 months, or with any adequacy item 'Sometimes' or 'Never'. Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

info.short_name: Continuously and adequately insured - suppressed flag
info.long_name: NSCH: SM_Adequate Insurance: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who are continuously and adequately insured - suppressed flag
info.short_description: 1 if nsch_pct_adequately_insured is suppressed because its unweighted denominator is below 30; 0 otherwise.
info.long_description: 1 when the measure applies to this year and age group but fewer than 30 sampled children are in the denominator, following the NSCH Comprehensive Analytic Guide (Data Presentation Standards: 'only presenting statistics with a sample size or unweighted denominator of 30 or more is recommended'). nsch_pct_adequately_insured and its CI are then NA. Not imputed.

info.short_name: Continuously and adequately insured - poor reliability flag
info.long_name: NSCH: SM_Adequate Insurance: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who are continuously and adequately insured - poor reliability flag
info.short_description: 1 if the 95% CI of nsch_pct_adequately_insured is wider than 20 percentage points or 1.2 times the estimate; 0 otherwise; NA if no estimate.
info.long_description: Flag following the NSCH Comprehensive Analytic Guide (Data Presentation Standards): 'if the 95% confidence interval width exceeds 20 percentage points or 1.2 times the estimate (relative standard error>30%), flagging the estimate for poor reliability ... is recommended'. The estimate is still reported. When the estimate is exactly 0 or 100 the logit CI is undefined: the CI columns are NA and, as a PopHIVE convention (not part of the Census guidance), the estimate is flagged 1.

info.short_name: Continuously and adequately insured - not-asked flag
info.long_name: NSCH: SM_Adequate Insurance: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who are continuously and adequately insured - not asked / not applicable flag
info.short_description: 1 if nsch_pct_adequately_insured is not available for this year and age group (outside the measure's universe or years); 0 otherwise.
info.long_description: 1 when no child in the national sample for this year and age group has a valid value for the measure: the age group is outside the measure's universe (Children ages 0-17), or the Title V code does not compute the measure for that year. nsch_pct_adequately_insured is then NA.

info.short_name: Housing instability in past year, ages 0-11
info.long_name: NSCH: NPM_Housing Instability: Percent of children, ages 0 through 11, who experienced housing instability in the past year
info.short_description: NPM_Housing Instability: Percent of children, ages 0 through 11, who experienced housing instability in the past year.
info.long_description: Weighted percent of children in the universe (Children ages 0-11) meeting the Title V definition 'NPM_Housing Instability: Percent of children, ages 0 through 11, who experienced housing instability in the past year' (National Performance Measure (NPM); Title V code variable Housing_0to11). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): EVERHOMELESS (SINCE this child WAS BORN, have they ever been homeless or lived in a shelter?), MISSMORTGAGE (DURING THE PAST 12 MONTHS, was there a time when you were not able to pay the mortgage or rent on time?), and PLACESLIVED (2022-2023) / MOVES (2024 onward: DURING THE PAST 12 MONTHS, how many times has this child moved to a new address?). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: ever homeless or lived in a shelter (EVERHOMELESS = Yes), or not able to pay the mortgage or rent on time in the past 12 months (MISSMORTGAGE = Yes), or moved 2 or more times in the past 12 months (MOVES = 3; PLACESLIVED = 2 in 2022-2023). Denominator adds children with none of these ('Don't Know' and missing items do not count as instability). Measure starts with 2022 data (Title V code: '2022 data forward'). Title V code comment: '2024 question/code change PLACESLIVED to MOVES'. Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: SC_CSHCN = 1 (qualifies on the CSHCN screener) or the child has 1 or more of the listed current conditions and 1 or more of the listed difficulties. (Very well or Somewhat well)' (NSCH survey item, not a Title V measure). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): K8Q21 (How well can you and this child share ideas or talk about things that really matter? 1=Very well; 2=Somewhat well; 3=Not very well; 4=Not well at all). Asked of children 6-17 (topical forms T2 and T3). Coding: Numerator: K8Q21 = 1 or 2 (Very well or Somewhat well). Denominator: K8Q21 = 1-4 (Very well, Somewhat well, Not very well, Not well at all). Missing responses are excluded. Not a Title V measure: the share of valid responses in the item's top two categories, reported directly. The item is on every year's file from 2016 with the same four codes. Variable lists: 2016-2017 ask 'How well can you and (fill with SC_NAME) share ideas ...' with option 4 labeled 'Not at all'; 2018 onward ask '... you and this child ...' with option 4 'Not well at all'. The Data Resource Center for Child and Adolescent Health lists a related indicator, 6.6 'Family shares ideas, 6-17 years'. Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

info.short_description: Flourishing for children and adolescents, age 6-17 years: Meets all 3 flourishing items.
info.long_description: Weighted percent of children in the universe (Children ages 6-17) meeting the Title V definition 'Flourishing for children and adolescents, age 6-17 years: Meets all 3 flourishing items' (Top category of a Title V code variable; Title V code variable flrish6to17). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): K6Q71_R (How often does this child ... Show interest and curiosity in learning new things? Always/Usually/Sometimes/Never); K7Q84_R (How often does this child ... Work to finish tasks they start? Always/Usually/Sometimes/Never); K7Q85_R (How often does this child ... Stay calm and in control when faced with a challenge? Always/Usually/Sometimes/Never). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: 'Always' or 'Usually' on all three items (the Title V code's count of 'Always' or 'Usually' responses equals 3). An unanswered item counts as not met; children with all three items missing are excluded. The Title V code restricts flourishing to data years 2018 onward; 2016-2017 are not reported. This is the 'Meets all 3 flourishing items' category reported by the Data Resource Center for Child and Adolescent Health (childhealthdata.org) for indicator 2.4; pooling 2022 and 2023 with this coding reproduces the DRC national value of 60.4% (39,696 sampled children meeting all 3). Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

info.short_description: NOM_Adolescent Depression/Anxiety: Percent of adolescents, ages 12 through 17, who have depression or anxiety.
info.long_description: Weighted percent of children in the universe (Adolescents ages 12-17) meeting the Title V definition 'NOM_Adolescent Depression/Anxiety: Percent of adolescents, ages 12 through 17, who have depression or anxiety' (National Outcome Measure (NOM); Title V code variable DepAnx_12to17). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): K2Q32B (Depression: If yes [a doctor or other health care provider EVER told you], does this child CURRENTLY have the condition?); K2Q33B (Anxiety Problems: If yes [a doctor or other health care provider EVER told you], does this child CURRENTLY have these problems?). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: currently has anxiety problems (K2Q33B = Yes) or currently has depression (K2Q32B = Yes). Children never diagnosed (logical skip) or not currently affected count in the denominator; children missing both items are excluded. Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

info.short_description: SM_Adequate Insurance: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who are continuously and adequately insured.
info.long_description: Weighted percent of children in the universe (Children ages 0-17) meeting the Title V definition 'SM_Adequate Insurance: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who are continuously and adequately insured' (Standardized State Performance Measure (SM); Title V code variable AdqIns). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): CURRINS (currently insured), INSGAP (insured all 12 months / with gaps / no coverage past 12 months), K3Q20 (How often does this child's health insurance offer benefits or cover services that meet this child's needs?), K3Q22 (How often does this child's health insurance allow them to see the health care providers they need?), HOWMUCH (out-of-pocket amount paid for this child's care in the past 12 months) and K3Q21B (How often are these costs reasonable?). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: insured all 12 months (INSGAP = 1) and insurance adequate, i.e. benefits (K3Q20) and access to providers (K3Q22) 'Always' or 'Usually' meet needs, and out-of-pocket costs (K3Q21B) 'Always' or 'Usually' reasonable or no out-of-pocket costs (HOWMUCH = $0); an item that is missing does not disqualify. Denominator adds children currently uninsured, uninsured at any point in the past 12 months, or with any adequacy item 'Sometimes' or 'Never'. Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

info.long_description: Unweighted count of NSCH respondents in the measure's denominator for this geography, year and demographic cell; this is the 'unweighted denominator' to which the NSCH Analytic Guide presentation standard applies. Weighted percent of children in the universe (Children ages 0-17) meeting the Title V definition 'SM_Smoking, Household: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who live in households where someone smokes' (Standardized State Performance Measure (SM); Title V code variable HHSmoking). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): K9Q40 (Does anyone living in your household use cigarettes, cigars, or pipe tobacco?). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: K9Q40 = Yes. Denominator: K9Q40 = Yes or No. Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

info.short_name: Lives in a household where someone smokes - suppressed flag
info.long_name: NSCH: SM_Smoking, Household: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who live in households where someone smokes - suppressed flag

info.long_description: 1 when the measure applies to this year and age group but fewer than 30 sampled children are in the denominator, following the NSCH Comprehensive Analytic Guide (Data Presentation Standards: 'only presenting statistics with a sample size or unweighted denominator of 30 or more is recommended'). nsch_pct_household_smoking and its CI are then NA. Not imputed.

info.short_name: Lives in a household where someone smokes - poor reliability flag
info.long_name: NSCH: SM_Smoking, Household: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who live in households where someone smokes - poor reliability flag
info.short_description: 1 if the 95% CI of nsch_pct_household_smoking is wider than 20 percentage points or 1.2 times the estimate; 0 otherwise; NA if no estimate.
info.long_description: Flag following the NSCH Comprehensive Analytic Guide (Data Presentation Standards): 'if the 95% confidence interval width exceeds 20 percentage points or 1.2 times the estimate (relative standard error>30%), flagging the estimate for poor reliability ... is recommended'. nsch_pct_flourishing_6_17.short_description: Flourishing for children and adolescents, age 6-17 years: Meets all 3 flourishing items.
nsch_pct_flourishing_6_17.long_description: Weighted percent of children in the universe (Children ages 6-17) meeting the Title V definition 'Flourishing for children and adolescents, age 6-17 years: Meets all 3 flourishing items' (Top category of a Title V code variable; Title V code variable flrish6to17). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): K6Q71_R (How often does this child ... Show interest and curiosity in learning new things? Always/Usually/Sometimes/Never); K7Q84_R (How often does this child ... Work to finish tasks they start? Always/Usually/Sometimes/Never); K7Q85_R (How often does this child ... Stay calm and in control when faced with a challenge? Always/Usually/Sometimes/Never). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: 'Always' or 'Usually' on all three items (the Title V code's count of 'Always' or 'Usually' responses equals 3). An unanswered item counts as not met; children with all three items missing are excluded. The Title V code restricts flourishing to data years 2018 onward; 2016-2017 are not reported. This is the 'Meets all 3 flourishing items' category reported by the Data Resource Center for Child and Adolescent Health (childhealthdata.org) for indicator 2.4; pooling 2022 and 2023 with this coding reproduces the DRC national value of 60.4% (39,696 sampled children meeting all 3). Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

nsch_pct_bullied_12_17_lcl.long_description: Lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for nsch_pct_bullied_12_17. Weighted percent of children in the universe (Adolescents ages 12-17) meeting the Title V definition 'NPM_Bullied, All Kids: Percent of adolescents, with and without special health care needs, ages 12 through 17, who are bullied' (National Performance Measure (NPM); Title V code variable AreBullied). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): BULLIED_R (DURING THE PAST 12 MONTHS, how often was this child bullied, picked on, or excluded by other children? Never/1-2 times/1-2 times per month/1-2 times per week/Almost every day). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: bullied, picked on, or excluded 1-2 times or more in the past 12 months (BULLIED_R = 2-5). Denominator adds 'Never' (BULLIED_R = 1). Measure starts with 2018 data (Title V code: 'Bullied or bully others ... 2018 onward'). Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

nsch_pct_aces_2plus.short_name: Two or more adverse childhood experiences
nsch_pct_aces_2plus.long_name: NSCH: NOM_Adverse Childhood Experiences: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who have experienced 2 or more ACEs
nsch_pct_aces_2plus.short_description: NOM_Adverse Childhood Experiences: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who have experienced 2 or more ACEs.
nsch_pct_aces_2plus.long_description: Weighted percent of children in the universe (Children ages 0-17) meeting the Title V definition 'NOM_Adverse Childhood Experiences: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who have experienced 2 or more ACEs' (National Outcome Measure (NOM); Title V code variable ACE2). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): ACE1 (SINCE THIS CHILD WAS BORN, how often has it been very hard to cover the basics, like food or housing, on your family's income? counted if Somewhat often or Very often) and ACE3-ACE11 (To the best of your knowledge, has this child EVER experienced: parent or guardian divorced or separated; parent or guardian died; parent or guardian served time in jail or prison; saw or heard parents or adults slap, hit, kick, punch one another in the home; was a victim of violence or witnessed violence in their neighborhood; lived with anyone who was mentally ill, suicidal, or severely depressed; lived with anyone who had a problem with alcohol or drugs; treated or judged unfairly because of their race or ethnic group; treated or judged unfairly because of a health condition or disability). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: two or more of the adverse childhood experiences listed (hard to cover basics counts when 'Somewhat often' or 'Very often'; each other item counts when 'Yes'). Answered items are counted even if others are missing; children missing every item are excluded. Title V code comments: ACE5 wording added 'or prison' in 2021; ACE11 (treated unfairly because of a health condition) was added in 2021, so 2016-2020 counts are out of 9 items. Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

nsch_pct_adequately_insured.long_name: NSCH: SM_Adequate Insurance: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who are continuously and adequately insured
nsch_pct_adequately_insured.short_description: SM_Adequate Insurance: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who are continuously and adequately insured.
nsch_pct_adequately_insured.long_description: Weighted percent of children in the universe (Children ages 0-17) meeting the Title V definition 'SM_Adequate Insurance: Percent of children, ages 0 through 17, who are continuously and adequately insured' (Standardized State Performance Measure (SM); Title V code variable AdqIns). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): CURRINS (currently insured), INSGAP (insured all 12 months / with gaps / no coverage past 12 months), K3Q20 (How often does this child's health insurance offer benefits or cover services that meet this child's needs?), K3Q22 (How often does this child's health insurance allow them to see the health care providers they need?), HOWMUCH (out-of-pocket amount paid for this child's care in the past 12 months) and K3Q21B (How often are these costs reasonable?). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: insured all 12 months (INSGAP = 1) and insurance adequate, i.e. benefits (K3Q20) and access to providers (K3Q22) 'Always' or 'Usually' meet needs, and out-of-pocket costs (K3Q21B) 'Always' or 'Usually' reasonable or no out-of-pocket costs (HOWMUCH = $0); an item that is missing does not disqualify. Denominator adds children currently uninsured, uninsured at any point in the past 12 months, or with any adequacy item 'Sometimes' or 'Never'. Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

nsch_pct_housing_instability_0_11.long_name: NSCH: NPM_Housing Instability: Percent of children, ages 0 through 11, who experienced housing instability in the past year
nsch_pct_housing_instability_0_11.short_description: NPM_Housing Instability: Percent of children, ages 0 through 11, who experienced housing instability in the past year.
nsch_pct_housing_instability_0_11.long_description: Weighted percent of children in the universe (Children ages 0-11) meeting the Title V definition 'NPM_Housing Instability: Percent of children, ages 0 through 11, who experienced housing instability in the past year' (National Performance Measure (NPM); Title V code variable Housing_0to11). Source items (2025 NSCH Topical Variable List wording): EVERHOMELESS (SINCE this child WAS BORN, have they ever been homeless or lived in a shelter?), MISSMORTGAGE (DURING THE PAST 12 MONTHS, was there a time when you were not able to pay the mortgage or rent on time?), and PLACESLIVED (2022-2023) / MOVES (2024 onward: DURING THE PAST 12 MONTHS, how many times has this child moved to a new address?). Coding (from the Title V code): Numerator: ever homeless or lived in a shelter (EVERHOMELESS = Yes), or not able to pay the mortgage or rent on time in the past 12 months (MISSMORTGAGE = Yes), or moved 2 or more times in the past 12 months (MOVES = 3; PLACESLIVED = 2 in 2022-2023). Denominator adds children with none of these ('Don't Know' and missing items do not count as instability). Measure starts with 2022 data (Title V code: '2022 data forward'). Title V code comment: '2024 question/code change PLACESLIVED to MOVES'. Single-year estimates from the NSCH public-use topical file, weighted with FWC; variance uses strata FIPSST x STRATUM and PSU HHID with domain estimation, and the 95% CI is logit-transformed. Rows with age = 'Overall' cover the full universe. Values are NA when suppressed or not asked (see the companion flag columns).

nsch.name: National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH)
nsch.organization: Health Resources and Services Administration, Maternal and Child Health Bureau (HRSA MCHB); conducted by the U.S. Census Bureau
nsch.location: NSCH public-use topical data files (Stata), 2016 onward, and the Title V measure code (SAS, 2016-2025)
nsch.description: The NSCH is an annual, cross-sectional, address-based household survey that produces national and state-level data on the physical and emotional health of children ages 0-17 in the United States. A parent or caregiver familiar with the child's health answers by web or mailed paper questionnaire about one randomly selected child in the household. It is sponsored by HRSA's Maternal and Child Health Bureau and conducted by the U.S. Census Bureau, and was redesigned in 2016; the Census Bureau advises that estimates from 2016 onward should not be compared with earlier NSCH surveys. Survey weights represent the non-institutionalized population of children residing in housing units in each state and DC. PopHIVE computes the estimates here from the public-use topical microdata: measures are coded with the Title V measure code that the Census Bureau publishes with the data files (or, for the few measures marked as NSCH survey items, as a single response category of one question), and are weighted single-year percentages with 95% logit confidence intervals that account for the survey design. Following the NSCH Comprehensive Analytic Guide, estimates with an unweighted denominator under 30 are suppressed and estimates whose 95% CI is wider than 20 percentage points or 1.2 times the estimate are flagged as unreliable. Single-year state estimates for small subgroups (for example, some race/ethnicity groups) are often suppressed or unreliable; the Census Bureau notes that multiple years can be combined for more precision. All responses are parent/caregiver reported. Time is the survey (data) year, coded YYYY-12-31; data collection for a survey year can extend into the following calendar year.
nsch.restrictions: Public use data. Per the Census Bureau NSCH FAQ: 'Data users are free to produce and publish works based on the NSCH data and documentation; proper attribution to the NSCH source material should accompany these works.' Suggested citation: Health Resources and Services Administration, Maternal and Child Health Bureau. [Year] National Survey of Children's Health Public Use Microdata File, STATA. Administered by the U.S. Census Bureau.
